title: How the studio takes clients and deferred payment
summary: He explains paid sessions versus demos billed only if placed with a label.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: If you don't object, I'd like to ask you a couple things about how you run the studio. There seems, from what I hear, there's like some sort of different systems. If somebody wants to come in here, pay you for the time, the studio's open to them. You know, so... Bonnie Raitt's recorded here. Paul McCartney's been here. King Biscuit Boy. The Mighty Diamonds. Robert Palmer. And so that's one aspect of the studio. Like, the musician can come here and pay you for the sessions. And you produce... And you produce the sound. And then the other system seems to be... And this, I think, applies to a lot of local musicians, is that... Since most of them don't have a lot of money, they can come in here and record. And they don't pay you unless the record actually sells.

Unless it can be placed somewhere and they can be reimbursed. For instance, if there's a group and they're not with anyone, they can come in and make a demo session or just record a session. And the studio bill will be calculated, but not issued to them. Then if they want to take it somewhere and try to place it with the company, let someone hear it and see if someone accepts it, they can do that. And if they find someone that accepts it, who will give them fronts, you might call it, which is only to reimburse what they've paid. Then they could pay the studio bill. Or if the company would take it and not give them any fronts, well then we'd wait and if the record sells, then they would collect anything.
Get paid. Do you and Marshall try to find record labels for some of the local musicians?
Sometime, yes. When folks seek that service, yes.
So it seems like you have a very open philosophy about just trying to make the studio available for different people with different needs.
Through that you can find what various, if there's talent that can't afford to in other ways, you can always seek that out. At least hear it.
